inspection.check.host.hdd.desc: Check the health status, IO utilization, and bad sectors of HDDs of hosts on the Cloud.
inspection.check.host.hdd.suggestion.war:
The HDDs of some hosts are in warning state. This may cause data reads and writes of VM instances on the hosts to get stuck and affect application workloads running on the VM instances. Troubleshooting: 

1.Health Status: If the health status of host HDDs is abnormal, check whether there are bad disk sectors, contact failures, or other faults, and change faulted disks if necessary. 

2.IO Utilization: If the HDD IO utilization has kept no less than 90% for 5 minutes, check whether the disk IO latency of related hosts is excessively too high, disk IO performance is deteriorated, and whether there are other exceptions. If disks are faulted, change the disks as needed. 

3.Bad Disk Sector: If there are bad disk sectors, check the disk IO of related hosts and the coverage of the faults and change the hardware as soon as possible.
inspection.check.host.memory.load.desc: Check the memory utilization, SWAP utilization, and ECC warnings of hosts on the Cloud.
inspection.check.host.memory.load.sugges:
The memory of some hosts are in warning state. This may cause host OOM errors, deteriorate host performance, and interrupt application workloads running on VM instances. Troubleshooting:
1. Memory Utilization: If the host memory utilization is no less than 90%, check the VM workloads running on related hosts. If the workloads are too heavy, migrate some VM instances to other hosts. If the workloads are in normal level, go to the host system and check whether memory leak occurs due to abnormal processes. 
2. SWAP Utilization: If host SWAP utilization is no less than 10%, check the status of VM instances running on related hosts, and migrate some VM instances and increase host memory if necessary. 
3. ECC Warning: If ECC warning occurs, check the status of VM instances running on related hosts and migrate some VM instances if necessary. In addition, check if memory fault errors. If so, change the host memory as soon as possible.
inspection.check.host.net.dev.desc: Check the NIC status, connection mode, packet loss rate, speed, and duplex mode of host NICs.
inspection.check.host.net.dev.suggestion:
The NICs of some hosts are in warning or fault state. This may affect data transmissions of business networks and VM data reads and writes. Troubleshooting:

1.NIC Status: If a host NIC is in DOWN state, check whether failures occur to related network hardware, including NICs, cables,optical modules, optical fibers. 
2.Packet Loss Rate: If the NIC packet loss rate is no lower than 10%, check whether related host NICs or switches work as expected and whether IP conflict errors occur.

3.NIC Connection Mode: If the negotiated port speed of a host NIC is lower than the rated port speed, it may be because of network hardware failures or lower-than-expected speed of uplink ports on the switch. Check the health status of related network hardware.

4.Full Duplex Mode: If a host NIC is not in full duplex mode, it may be because of configuration errors of the uplink switch port or network hardware failures such as the NIC or network cable. Check whether these network devices are in good health status and whether the configurations of related uplink switch ports are correct. You can also manually set the mode to full duplex as needed.

5.Port Speed: If the port speed is lower than 1Gps, it may cause insufficient network performance. We recommend that you use NICs with port speed higher than 1Gps.

The NICs of some hosts are in warning state. This may cause host disconnection and affect data transmissions of business networks. Troubleshooting:

1.Packet Loss Rate: If the NIC packet loss rate is no lower than 0.1%, it may be because there are network fluctuations or network hardware failures. Check whether related host NICs or switches work as expected.

2.NIC Connection Mode: If the negotiated port speed of a host NIC is lower than the rated port speed, it may be because of network hardware failures or lower-than-expected speed of uplink ports on the switch. Check the health status of related network hardware.

3.Full Duplex Mode: If a host NIC is not in full duplex mode, it may be because of configuration errors of the uplink switch port or network hardware failures such as the NIC or network cable. Check whether these network hardware devices are in good health status and whether the configurations of related uplink switch ports are correct. You can also manually set the mode to full duplex as needed.

4.Port Speed: If the port speed is lower than 1Gps, it may cause insufficient network performance. We recommend that you use NICs with port speed higher than 1Gps.
inspection.check.host.raid.state.desc: Check the RAID card status and cache mode of hosts on the Cloud.
inspection.check.host.raid.state.suggest: Exceptions occur to some host RAID cards, which  may be because of RAID card faults or contact failures and may cause host system hangs and VM I/O stuck. Check whether related host RAID cards are in good health status and check whether there are warnings on RAID card failures on the out-of-band management interface. If there are RAID card failures, change the RAID cards as soon as possible.

Some host RAID cards are in a Degraded state or use a cache mode other than write-through.

- Degraded state: This may affect the data redundancy. Check the health state of the RAID cards and process this problem as soon as possible.

- Cache mode other than write-through: This may make storage services unable to be launched and data on the system volume unable to be resumed in case of a power outage. Reset the cache mode of related host RAID cards to write-through.
inspection.check.host.real.cpu.status.de: Check the status and temperature of every host CPU on the Cloud.
inspection.check.host.real.cpu.status.su: The CPU of some hosts is offline. This may cause hosts to run unstably, auto power off or restart, and thus interrupt application workloads running on VM instances.

The CPU temperature of some hosts has kept no lower than 80℃ for 5 minutes. Sustained high temperature may cause hosts to run unstably, auto power off or restart, and thus interrupt application workloads running on VM instances. Troubleshooting:
- Check whether the temperature of the machine room has exceeded the higher threshold required for the stable running of hosts.
- Check the out-of-band management interface whether warnings are triggered because of low rotation speed of the fan, or the fault of the CPU or motherboard.

inspection.check.host.ssd.desc: Check the health status, IO utilization, remaining life expectancy, and temperature of SSDs of hosts on the Cloud.
inspection.check.host.ssd.life.left.desc: Check Remaining Life Expectancy of SSD Used by Distributed Storage.
inspection.check.host.ssd.suggestion.cri:
The SSDs of some hosts are in warning or fault state. Troubleshooting:

1.Temperature: If the SSD temperature of hosts is no lower than 70℃, check whether the temperature of the machine room is too high and whether there are sustained and intensive data writes on the SSDs. High temperature may cause SSDs to run unstably and affect data reads and writes of VM instances.

2.Remaining Life Expectancy: If the remaining life expectancy of an SSD is lower than 10% , replace the SSD with an SSD of the same specification. Otherwise, the SSD may be faulted and data reads and writes are terminated. 

3.IO Utilization: If the SSD IO utilization has kept no less than 90% for 5 minutes, check whether the disk IO latency is excessively too high, disk IO performance is deteriorated, and whether there are other exceptions. Sustained high IO utilization may cause application workloads on VM instances to get stuck.
inspection.check.host.ssd.suggestion.war:
The SSDs of some hosts are in warning state. Troubleshooting:

1.Health Status: If the health status of host SSDs is abnormal, check whether there are disk faults and change the faulted SSDs as soon as possible. Abnormal health status of SSDs may cause data reads and writes of VM instances to get stuck or even system hangs.

2.IO Utilization: If the SSD IO utilization has kept no less than 90% for 5 minutes, check whether the disk IO latency is excessively too high, disk IO performance is deteriorated, and whether there are other exceptions. Sustained high IO utilization may cause application workloads on VM instances to get stuck.

3.Temperature: If the SSD temperature of hosts is equal to or higher than 60℃ and lower than 70℃, check whether there are sustained and intensive data writes on the SSDs. High temperature may cause SSDs to run unstably and affect data reads and writes of VM instances.

4.Remaining Life Expectancy: If the remaining life expectancy of an SSD is no lower than 10% yet no higher than 30%, replace the SSD with an SSD of the same specification. Otherwise, when the remaining life expectancy of the SSD decreases to 0, data reads and writes are terminated.

instanceOffering.field.allocatorStrategy:
### Host Allocation Strategy
1. When you create a VM instance by using this instance offering, the system will allocate a host for the VM instance according to the chosen host allocation strategy.

    - Host with min. running VMs: The host with the minimum number of running VM instances will be chosen to create VM instances.
    - Host with min. CPU utilization: The host with the minimum CPU utilization will be chosen to create VM instances.
    - Host with min. memory utilization: The host with the minimum memory utilization will be chosen to create VM instances.
    - Host with max. running VMs: The host with the maximum number of running VM instances will be chosen to create VM instances. To use this option, you need to set the maximum number of VM instances that can run on a host. Then, the system chooses the host that meets the requirements to create VM instances. If no host is available, you would fail to create a VM instance.
    - Host where the VM located last time: When you restart a stopped VM instance, the system chooses the host where the VM was running last time. If you start a new VM instance for the first time, the system chooses a host randomly.
    - Random allocation: The system randomly chooses a host to create VM instances.

2. If you choose the "Host with min. CPU utilization" or "Host with min. memory utilization" strategy, you can set the interval for collecting the CPU utilization and memory utilization in the global settings.

instanceOffering.field.strategyPattern.t:
### Strategy Pattern

 1. If the cloud can query the host load information, the cloud creates VM instances according to the host allocation strategy.
2. If the cloud cannot query the host load information, the cloud creates VM instances according to the following strategy patterns:
    - Allocation strategy (soft): The cloud randomly allocates a host with sufficient resources to create VM instances without considering the host allocation strategy
    - Allocation strategy (hard): The cloud uses the host allocation strategy forcibly, which might cause VM creation failure.

interface.field.serviceTypes.iconTooltip:
### Physical Network Type
Attach tags to the physical NIC port to mark which network type it serves, including the management network, storage network, business network, backup network, and migration network.

1. Management network:

   - A network used to manage physical resources on the Cloud. Management nodes use a management network to access hots, primary storage, backup storage, VPC vRouter, and LB instances (dedicated-performance).

   - The management network tag is attached to corresponding ports automatically by the system. You cannot attach/detach this tag to/from a NIC port by yourself.

2. Storage network: A network specified for storage services. The Cloud uses a storage network to get the health status of virtual machines. We recommend that you deploy a dedicated storage network to avoid possible risks.

3. Business Network: A network that can be added as L2/L3 network on the Cloud and attached to virtual machines. A virtual machine uses a business network to provide services.

4. Backup Network: A network used to back up or recover local business data in a local backup scenario. A dedicated backup network is necessary if you use Backup Service.

5. Migration Network: A network used for VM migration on the Cloud.

### DHCP IP

1. A DHCP IP is an IP address occupied by the DHCP service. The DHCP service assigns IP addresses to virtual machines in this L3 network by using the DHCP IP.
2. If you create an L3 network for the first time with the DHCP service enabled, or add the first network range to an L3 network with the DHCP service enabled, you can customize the DHCP IP.
3. If the L3 network has a DHCP IP, you could not customize the DHCP IP when you add a network range.
4. The DHCP IP can be in or outside the added IP range, but it must be an unoccupied IP address in the CIDR block of the added IP range.
5. If not specified, the system would randomly assign an IP address from within the added IP range.
ipRange.modal.delete.alert.danger:
1. Deleting a network range detaches the VM NICs that are using the network range. If the NIC is using a double-stack network, it is detached only when both the IPv4 and IPv6 ranges it is using are deleted.
2. Deleting a network range deletes the VPC vRouters whose default public network NICs are using the network range. If the NIC is using a double-stack network, the VPC vRouter is deleted only when both the IPv4 and IPv6 ranges the NIC is using are deleted.
3. Deleting a network range deletes the VPC vRouters whose management network NICs are using the network range. If the NIC is using a double-stack network, the VPC vRouter is deleted only when both the IPv4 and IPv6 ranges the NIC is using are deleted. 
4. If the L3 network has a DHCP IP that is in the selected network range, deleting the network range does not delete the DHCP IP. If all network ranges under the L3 network are deleted, the DHCP IP will be released.

l2Network.networkAccelerationMode.toolti:
### Switch Type

Switches are responsible for connecting VM instances to the physical network. Supported types include Linux Bridge and OVS-DPDK.

* Linux Bridge: The Linux Bridge switch type is suitable for small-scale, low-load network environments.
* OVS-DPDK: The OVS-DPDK switch type is designed for high-performance and low-latency network environments.
l2Network.physicalInterface.tips: You can only select or enter a NIC name shared across all hosts in the cluster, for example, eth0.
l2Network.type.tooltip:
### Network Type

The following L2 network types are supported:

#### L2NoVlanNetwork

1. You must specify the NIC name of the host.
2. The hosts in the cluster to which the L2 network is attached must have NICs that share the same name.
3. When the data packets of VM instances flow out of the host NIC and reach the physical switch, the data packets are not flagged with VLAN tags. Note that the physical switch must be in VLAN Access mode.
4. If you create an L2 network of the L2NoVlanNetwork type, a network bridge is created based on the specified host NIC.

#### L2VlanNetwork  

1. You must specify the host NIC name and VLAN ID.
2. The hosts in the cluster to which the L2 network is attached must have NICs that share the same name.
3. When the data packets of VM instances flow out of the host NIC and reach the physical switch, the data packets are tagged with the specified VLAN ID.
4. If you create an L2 network of the L2VlanNetwork type, a VLAN device is created based on the specified VLAN ID and then a network bridge is created based on the VLAN device.
5. If you attach an L2 network of the L2NoVlanNetwork type and an L2 network of the L2VlanNetwork type or attach multiple L2 networks of the L2VlanNetwork type to a cluster, the physical switch NIC must be in Trunk mode. Besides, the VLAN ID in use must be contained in the Trunk VLAN configurations.

#### VxlanNetwork  

1. Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN) is an overlay technology that allows for the creation of overlaying L2 networks. This technology can support a maximum of 16 million logical networks.
2. VxlanNetwork is an implementation of the software-based VXLAN technology.
3. If you create an L2 network of the VxlanNetwork type, you must specify a software SDN-based VXLAN pool. The L2 network must correspond to a VNI in the pool.
4. The VTEP IPs of the hosts in the cluster to which the L2 network of the VxlanNetwork type is attached must belong to the specified VXLAN pool.
5. When the data packets of VM instances flow out of the host, the host encapsulates VXLAN messages to the data packets and then sends the encapsulated data to the physical switch.

#### HardwareVxlanNetwork   

1. Virtual Extensible LAN (VXLAN) is an overlay technology that allows for the creation of overlaying L2 networks. This technology can support a maximum of 16 million logical networks.
2. HardwareVxlanNetwork is a solution to the integration with third-party hardware SDN.
3. Make sure a valid SDN network license is added to the platform.
4. If you create an L2 network of the HardwareVxlanNetwork type, you must specify a hardware SDN-based VXLAN pool. The L2 network must correspond to a VNI in the pool.
5. When the data packets of VM instances flow out of the host NICs and reach the distributed virtual switches, the data packets are flagged with the specified VLAN ID. The VLAN ID is mapped with VXLAN ID based on the SDN controlled that you add to the Cloud.
l2Network.type.tooltip.case.wizard:
### L2 Network

Supported types:

#### L2NoVlanNetwork:

1. You must specify the NIC name of the host.
2. The hosts in the cluster to which the L2 network is attached must have NICs that share the same name.
3. When the data packets of VM instances flow out of the host NIC and reach the physical switch, the data packets are not flagged with VLAN tags. Note that the physical switch must be in VLAN Access mode.
4. If you create an L2 network of the L2NoVlanNetwork type, a network bridge is created based on the specified host NIC.

#### L2VlanNetwork:
1. You must specify the host NIC name and VLAN ID.
2. The hosts in the cluster to which the L2 network is attached must have NICs that share the same name.
3. When the data packets of VM instances flow out of the host NIC and reach the physical switch, the data packets are tagged with the specified VLAN ID.
4. If you create an L2 network of the L2VlanNetwork type, a VLAN device is created based on the specified VLAN ID and then a network bridge is created based on the VLAN device.
5. If you attach an L2 network of the L2NoVlanNetwork type and an L2 network of the L2VlanNetwork type or attach multiple L2 networks of the L2VlanNetwork type to a cluster, the physical switch NIC must be in Trunk mode. Besides, the VLAN ID in use must be contained in the Trunk VLAN configurations.

When you create an L2 network, make sure that:
The network device is available on the host in the cluster.

l3Network.field.ipAllocateStrategy.toolt:
### IP Allocation Policy

After enabling the DHCP service, you can select one of the following three allocation policies to assign IP addresses:

1. Random: The system randomly assigns IP addresses from the network range.  

2. Allocate in Order  
 - The system assigns all available IP addresses from the network range in ascending order. Released IP addresses are assigned in the next allocation.
- Example: Assume that the network range is 192.168.0.101～192.168.0.120, within which 192.168.0.101～192.168.0.108 are allocated. If 192.168.0.106 is released, it will be assigned first in the next allocation.

3. Allocate in Cycle  
 - The system assigns available IP addresses from the network range in ascending order. Released IP addresses are assigned when currently available IP addresses are used up.
- Example: Assume that the network range is 192.168.0.101～192.168.0.120, within which 192.168.0.101～192.168.0.108 are allocated. If 192.168.0.106 is released, it will be assigned after 192.168.0.120 is used.
l3Network.field.ipRangeMethod.ipv4.toolt:
### Network Range Method

Support 2 network range methods: IP Range
 and CIDR.

1. IP Range: Add an IP range from the start IP to the end IP. For example, you can set the start IP as 192.168.0.100, end IP as 192.168.0.200, netmask as 255.255.0.0, and gateway as 192.168.0.1. Do not include a gateway address, broadcast address, or network address in the IP range.

2.  CIDR: Classless Inter-Domain Routing. For example, you can set the CIDR as 192.168.0.0/24. We recommend that you set the gateway as the first or last address in the CIDR. If left blank, the gateway uses the first address by default.
l3Network.field.ipRangeMethod.ipv6.toolt:
### Network Range Method

1. IP range: provides an IP configuration method: Stateful-DHCP. For example, you can set the IP range to 3000:910A:2222:5498:8475:1111:3900:4002–3000:910A:2222:5498:8475:1111:3900:400f, prefix length to 64, and gateway to 3000:910A:2222:5498:8475:1111:3900:4001.
2. CIDR: provides three IP configuration methods: Stateful-DHCP, Stateless-DHCP, and SLAAC. For example, 236C:347A:4D::/64.

#### Notice:

1. If you use the Stateless-DHCP or SLAAC method, you need to manually change the IP generation method to EUI64.
2. The prefix length ranges from 64 to 126. If the value is smaller than 64, the VM creation might fail.
3. Do not include a gateway address (xxxx::1) in the IP range.
l3Network.field.ipRangeType.tooltip:
### Network Range Type

IPv4 public networks support address pools. You can add both normal network ranges and address pool network ranges at the same time.

#### Normal Network Range
1. You can add a normal network range via an IP range or a CIDR. Note that multiple network ranges must belong to the same CIDR.
     - IP Range: Add an IP range from the start IP to the end IP. For example, you can set the start IP as 192.168.0.100, end IP as 192.168.0.200, netmask as 255.255.0.0, and gateway as 192.168.0.1. Do not include a gateway address, broadcast address, or network address in the IP range.
     - CIDR: Classless Inter-Domain Routing. For example, you can set the CIDR as 192.168.0.0/24 and set the gateway as the first or last address in the CIDR. If not set, the gateway uses the first address by default.
2. A normal network range applies to all IP allocation scenarios.

#### Address Pool Network Range 
1. An address pool network range must co-exist with a normal network range. You could not add an address pool network range if no normal network range is available.
2. Make sure that the address pool network range is planned and configured as a public network. Otherwise, the network is unreachable.
3. You can add an address pool network range via an IP range. Multiple network ranges can locate in different CIDRs.
4. Do not include a broadcast address or network address in the address pool network range.
5. An address pool network range can be only used to create VIPs to provide network services.

### Data Compression

Default: disabled. When enabled, the system will compress files of specific types. Data compression reduces the size of transferred files, improves file transfer efficiency, and reduces bandwidth consumption.

listener.action.set.sessionPersistence:
### Session Persistence

1. An innate mechanism of the load balancing service. It identifies the association of the interactions between a client and backend servers based on which a load balancer can direct the client's requests to a specific backend server and achieve business continuity. 

2. The Cloud provides two session persistence mechanisms: TCP/UDP-based 4th-layer session persistence and HTTP/HTTPS-based 7th-layer session persistence.

- 4th-layer session persistence: A load balancer directs requests from clients of the same source IP address to a backend server.
- 7th-layer session persistence: The mechanisms under different load balancing algorithms differ from each other.

   - Round Robin and Weighted Round Robin apply cookie-based session persistence. A load balancer uses a cookie to direct the requests to the backend server previously responded.
   - Source IP Hash uses the Hash function to calculate the source IP addresses of clients and directs requests from clients of the same source IP address to a backend server.

3. Note:

- When you choose 4th-layer session persistence: If you select Source IP Hash for Load Balancer Algorithm, session persistence is enabled and cannot be disabled. If you select an algorithm other than Source IP Hash, session persistence is disabled and cannot be enabled.
- When you choose HTTP/HTTPS-based 7th-layer session persistence: If you select Source IP Hash for Load Balancer Algorithm, session persistence is enabled and cannot be disabled. If you select Least Connections, session persistence is disabled and cannot be enabled.
- When you choose HTTP-based 7th-layer session persistence: If you select Round Robin or Weighted Round Robin for Load Balancer Algorithm and choose Rewrite Cookie, the http-tunnel mode is not supported.

listener.dataCompressAlgorithm.label.too:
### Data Compression Algorithm

Default value: gzip.

- gzip: One of the most widely used HTTP content encoding method and is based on DEFLATE algorithm for compression.
- deflate: A specific compression algorithm actually applied to gzip and other compression formats and is a combination of the LZ77 (Lempel-Ziv) algorithm and Huffman coding.
- raw-delate: Compresses the data using only the DEFLATE algorithm without any additional header or footer information.

Note: When choosing deflate or raw-deflate, make sure that both the client and the backend server are able to handle these compression formats correctly, otherwise it may result in data not being decompressed or displaying abnormally.

 1. If the listening protocol is TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS, the health check protocol can be TCP or HTTP. If the listening protocol is UDP, the health check protocol can be UDP.
 2. If you select HTTP, you can configure the normal status code, health check URI, and health check method.

### Health Check URI

The URI of the page on which health checks are performed, for example, /healthcheck.html. A health check on static pages is recommended. When you set a health check URI, make sure that:
- The URI must be 2-80 characters in length.
- The URI can contain only letters, digits, hyphens (-), forward slashes (/), periods (.), percent signs (%), question marks (?), number signs (#), and ampersands (&).
- The URI must start with a forward slash (/) but cannot contain only forward slashes.
listener.field.healthyThreshold.tooltip:

listener.field.httpMode.tooltip:
### HTTP Mode

The HTTP connection mode of the load balacner. This option appears only when the listening protocol is HTTP.
 
- http-server-close: The server-facing connection is closed after the end of the response is received, and the client-facing connection remains open.
- http-keep-alive: All requests and responses are processed, and connections remain open but idle between responses and new requests.
- http-tunnel: Only the first request and response are processed and a tunnel is established between the client and the server, so that they can talk without further analysis of HTTP protocol. This mode is not recommended. Note that this mode does not support the HTTP session persistence mechanism that applies the Round Robin/Weighted Round Robin algorithm and Rewrite Cookie handling method.
- httpclose: The same as tunnel mode, but with a Connection: close header added in both the client and server directions. This mode is not recommended.
- forceclose: Both the client and the server connections are actively closed by the load balancer after the end of a response.

listener.field.httpRedirectHttps.tooltip:
### HTTP Redirect

Redirects all flows accessing the HTTP listener to an HTTPS listener.

1. Make sure that the current load balancer has an available HTTPS listener to process the redirected flows. Otherwise, create one first.

2. After you enable HTTP Redirect, other configurations of the HTTP listener become invalid, such as the health-checking parameters and forwarding rules. If these configurations are necessary, manually sync them to the destination HTTPS listener.

3. Disable Session Persistence before you can enable HTTP Redirect.

listener.field.nbprocess.tooltip:

2. Using multiple processes can improve the listener performance and the data concurrency. Howerver, multiple processes might occupy more memory and affect the monitoring accuracy.

listener.field.redirectPort.statusCode:
### Redirect Status Code

1. 301: Moved Permanently. Informs the client that the requested resource has been moved to a new address permanently. The client can cache and access the new address directly on the next request.

2. 302: Founds. Informs the client that the requested resource has been moved to a new address temporarily. The client does not cache this new address and still accesses the original address first on the next request.

3. 303: See Other. This code is similar to code 302, but the client must obtain the new address through a GET request. This code mainly applies to scenarios where you want to skip to a GET request after a POST request.

4. 307: Temporary Redirect. This code is similar to code 302, but the client's request method for accessing the new address must be the same as the request method for accessing the original address.

5. 308: Permanent Redirect. This code is similar to code 301, but the client's request method for accessing the new address must be the same as the request method for accessing the original address.
listener.field.securityPolicyType.toolti:
### TLS Security Policy

A Transport Layer Security (TLS) security policy includes a TLS version that can be selected for HTTPS and its associated cipher suites. Valid values:

- tls_cipher_policy_1_0: supports TLS 1.0 or later and its associated cipher suites. This security policy has the highest compatibility while is relatively less secure.
- tls_cipher_policy_1_1: supports TLS 1.1 or later and its associated cipher suites. This security policy has relatively higher compatibility and is relatively secure.
- tls_cipher_policy_1_2: supports TLS 1.2 or later and its associated cipher suites. This security policy has relatively higher compatibility and is quite secure.
- tls_cipher_policy_1_2_strict: supports TLS 1.2 or later and supports only forward secret cipher suites. This security policy is very secure.
- tls_cipher_policy_1_2_strict_with_1_3: supports TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 and supports only forward secret cipher suites. This security policy is very secure.

listener.loadBalancerAlgorithm:
### Load Balancer Algorithm

The algorithm a load balancer uses to forwards frontend traffic to backend servers. The following four algorithms are supported:

1. Round Robin: Forwards equal shares of traffic to backend servers in turn. It is the simplest load balancing algorithm, which does not consider server status and is mostly used when the performance of each backend server varies little.
2. Weighted Round Robin: Forwards the traffic to backend servers based on the static weight configured in most cases according to hardware configurations of the servers. Requests are more likely to be distributed to backend servers with a higher weight. Weighted round robin is a variant of the round robin algorithm and is mostly used when the performance of each backend server varies much.
3. Source IP Hash: Generates a hash based on the source and destination IP addresses and then forwards traffic to specific backend servers. This algorithm is applicable to scenarios when the requests of different clients vary much.
4. Least Connections: Forwards new connection requests to backend servers that record least connections. This algorithm is applicable to scenarios when the time that backend servers used to handle different requests varies much. It is often used for long-term connection services.

loadBalancer.field.backendNetwork.toolti:
### Backend Network

The network where the backend server that processes the frontend requests distributed by a load balancer is located.
 #### Shared-performance LB

 1. If you specify a public network as the frontend network, you can specify any one of the VPC networks of the VPC vRouter to which the public network is attached as the backend network.
 2. If you specify a VPC network as the frontend network, you can specify any one of the VPC networks of the VPC vRouter to which the VPC network is attached as the backend network.
 
 #### Dedicated-performance LB

 1. If you specify a public network as the frontend network, you can specify a flat network or any one of the VPC networks of the VPC vRouter to which the public network is attached as the backend network.
 2. If you specify a flat network as the frontend network, you must specify the same network as the backend network.
 3. If you specify a VPC network of a VPC vRouter as the frontend network, you must specify the same network as the backend network. If you need to associate the load balancer with more backend networks, you can attach more NICs to the load balancer instance. Note that the backend networks that you associate are among the other VPC networks of the VPC vRouter.

#### Severity Level (Lowest to Highest)

- ALL: Receive all log messages regardless of level.

- DEBUG: Detailed logs for debugging or troubleshooting.

- WARN (default): Indicates potential issues that do not affect normal operation.
- ERROR: Indicates an error that may impact normal operation.
- FATAL: Indicates a critical error that may cause the application to crash or become unable to continue.

md5Sum.tooltip:
### MD5

Calculate the MD5 value of an image uploaded to a virtualized platform for verification purposes. This can be used to confirm whether the uploaded image is complete and intact.

Note:
1. Only images uploaded via URL or local file support MD5 calculation.
2. Images in a distributed repository do not support MD5 calculation.
3. After uploading an image in VMDK format, it will be automatically converted. Therefore, the MD5 value obtained here cannot be used as a basis for verifying the integrity of the uploaded image.

### Message Source

1. A message source is used to take over third-party alarm messages. If you configure alarms for message sources, extended alarm messages can be sent to various endpoints. Currently, Ceph Enterprise is supported.

### Alarm Message Template

1. A message template specifies the text of a resource alarm message or event alarm message sent to an SNS system.
2. By default, the system provides an alarm message template and a recovery message template. If you did not create one, the default templates will be used.
3. You can create multiple message templates but make only one of them as default. Alarm messages are sent by using the format specified in the default template.

messageTemplate.field.type.tooltip:
### Type
1. Supports massage templates for Email, Alibaba Cloud SMS, Universal SMS, DingTalk, Lark, WeCom, Webhook, and Microsoft Teams. By using a message template, you can send messages in unified formats to endpoints.

2. Alibaba Cloud SMS message templates apply to SMS endpoints using Alibaba Cloud SMS service. Before you create an Alibaba Cloud SMS message template, apply for an SMS signature and template on Alibaba Cloud in advance. If you need to modify an existing Alibaba Cloud SMS template, make the modification on Alibaba Cloud and apply for a new signature, and then, sync the modification to the Cloud. Universal SMS message template apply to SMS endpoints using SMS services provided by other telecom operators.

3. To create an alarm message template, you need to follow the specific syntax rules based on the endpoint type. You can specify the information you need in the message template with the sample template below as a reference.

    a. To create an Email or Lark message template, follow the Text syntax.

    b. To create a DingTalk or WeCom message template, follow the Markdown syntax.

    c. To create a Webhook message template, follow the JSON syntax.

    d. To create a Microsoft Teams message template, follow the Webhook syntax requirements listed on the Microsoft Teams official website.
messageTemplate.field.type.tooltip.advan:
### Type

By using a message template, you can send messages in unified formats to endpoints.

1. To create an Email or Lark message template, follow the Text syntax.
2. To create a DingTalk or WeCom message template, follow the Markdown syntax.
3. To create a HTTP Application message template, follow the JSON syntax.
4. To create a Microsoft Teams message template, follow the Webhook syntax requirements listed on the Microsoft Teams official website.
5. To create a SMS message template, you need to apply for third-party SMS signatures templates in advance. Currently, you can use Alibaba Cloud SMS service. Any template changes require re-applying through the third-party service.
messageTemplate.field.type.tooltip.basic:

1. To create an Email message template, follow the Text syntax.
2. To create a HTTP Application message template, follow the JSON syntax.
3. To create a SMS message template, you need to apply for third-party SMS signatures templates in advance. Currently, you can use Alibaba Cloud SMS service. Any template changes require re-applying through the third-party service.

modify.dhcpService.modal.field.switch.in:
### DHCP Service

1. Enable DHCP service:

    - After enabled, you need to specify a DHCP server IP.
    - After enabled, VM instances in this L3 network may need to obtain IP addresses again, which may result in IP change. Proceed with caution.
    - If you have configured a static IP inside the VM instance before enabling the DHCP service and the VM instance does not install GuestTools, then after enabled, redistributing the IP will result in two IPs on the VM NIC. It is recommended to install GuestTools for VM instance in advance and read the IP configuration before enabling the DHCP service.

2. Disable DHCP service:

    - After disabled, if VM instances in this L3 network do not have static IP addresses, proceed with caution as these VM instances may encounter network disruptions upon reboot. It is recommended to install GuestTools for VM instance in advance, configure static IP addresses, and synchronize configurations.
    - After disabled, the VM instance will not be assigned an IP address when a new VM instance is created on the public network or flat network.

nic.monitorData.tooltip:
### Monitoring Data

Displays the NIC monitoring data within the selected time range by using cards and curve charts.

1. The cards show the total traffic, average/maximum data rate, and the 95th percentile of data sent or received by a NIC.

   - Total traffic: The total amount of data sent or received by a NIC.
   - Average data rate: The average amount of data sent or received per second by a NIC.
   - Maximum data rate: The maximum value of the average data rate. The average data rate is calculated every 5 minutes.
   - 95th percentile: This value is calculated by arranging the average data rate samples collected every 5 minutes in the selected time range in descending order, and removing all values greater than the highest 5% of the data.

2. The curve charts show the real-time NIC data rate and packet rate.

   - NIC data rate: The number of data bits sent or received by a NIC per second.
   - NIC packet rate: The number of data packets sent or received by a NIC per second.

The mode that the platform syncs time with a NTP server. The following modes are supported:

1. Internal: Uses a management node or host as the time server for the platform system time to synchronize time with other nodes on the platform. You can add a maximum of 2 internal time servers.

physicalNetwork.field.modify.physicalNet:
### Physical Network Type

Attach tags to the physical NIC port to mark which network type it serves. Network types include the management network, storage network, business network, backup network, migration network, and others.

Note: The management network tag is automatically attached to corresponding ports by the system. You cannot manually attach/detach this tag to/from a NIC port.

#### Management Network

A network used to manage physical resources on the Cloud. Management nodes use a management network to access hots, primary storage, image storage, VPC vRouter, and LB instances (dedicated-performance).


#### Storage Network

A network specified for storage services. The Cloud uses a storage network to get the health status of VM instances. We recommend that you deploy a dedicated storage network to avoid possible risks.

#### Business Network
A network that can be added as L2/L3 network on the Cloud and attached to VM instances. A VM instance uses a business network to provide services.

#### Backup Network

A network used to back up or recover local business data in a local backup scenario. A dedicated backup network is necessary if you use Backup Service.

#### Migration Network

A network used for VM migration on the Cloud.

#### Others

Other network types defined by yourself.
physicalNetwork.field.networkPort.column:

1. If you are marking NIC ports in batch, select ports that exist on each host above. For example, if you want to mark eth0, make sure that each host has a NIC port named eth0 installed. You can attach the same network type tags to all these eth0 on different hosts at once.
2. If you only want to mark a subnet port slaving to the physical NIC port, specify the corresponding VLAN ID. If no VLAN ID is specified, the entire NIC port is marked by default.
3. To NIC ports that have network type tags attached before, you cannot add/delete tags to/from them on this page. To add or delete tags, go to their action lists and click "Modify Network Type".

physicalNic.action.modal.lldp.mode.toolt:
### LLDP Mode

LLDP allows you to receive LLDP information from a neighboring network device, or to transmit the local LLDP information to its neighbors. With LLDP, you can query and judge the link communication status.

1. LLDP has the following 4 modes:

- Receive-only mode (Default): Processes received LLDP packets and displays LLDP information.
- Transmit-only mode: Transmits LLDP packets, and does not process received packets. You cannot view LLDP in this mode.
- Transmit and Receive mode: Performs both transmit and receive LLDP packet processing.
- Disabled: Do not transmit or receive LLDP packets. You cannot view LLDP in this mode. 

2. LLDP can work in the following OS:

-  x86: H84r and x86_KylinV10P3
- ARM: arm_KylinV10P3 and H22e

portForwarding.field.name.tooltip:
### Port Forwarding 
1. The firewall policy in the VM instances must be open to the specified forwarding port.    
2. A VIP can provide port forwarding services to different ports of multiple VM NICs on the same L3 network.
3. A port range is supported. Note that the VIP and VM NIC in the port range must map to the same port number.
portForwarding.field.port.tooltip:
### Port 
#### The following two port mapping methods are supported:
1. Specified port: port-to-port mapping.  

   - Source port: You can select a port from ports 1-65535 as the source port.    

   - VM port: You can select a port from ports 1-65535 as the VM port.  
 
   For example, if you set 24 as the source port and 22 as the VM port, the traffic to port 24 of the public IP will be forwarded to port 22 of the VM instance.   

2. Port range: You can select two ports from ports 1-65535 as the start port and end port, respectively.    
  
   For example, if the port range is 22-80, traffic to ports 22-80 of the public IP will be forwarded to ports 22-80 of the VM instance.
portForwarding.field.protocal.tooltip:
### Protocol

Select a protocol type, including TCP and UDP.

1. TCP: supports ports 1–65535.  
2. UDP: supports ports 1–65535.

portForwarding.glossary: Port forwarding functions based on the L3 forwarding service of VPC vRouters. This service forwards traffic flows of the specified IP address and port in the specified network to a port of VM instances by using the specified protocol. If your public IP addresses are insufficient, you can configure port forwarding for multiple VM instances by using one IP address and port.

Enabling port mirroring immediately after the creation may occupy physical network bandwidth. Make sure that your business is not affected and then select the checkbox.
portMirror.field.flowNetwork.tooltip:
### Flow Network

1. A flow network is a dedicated network for port mirroring. You can use a flow network to transmit the mirrors of data packets of NIC ports to the target ports.
2. You cannot use a flow netwok for other purposes except for port mirroring.
3. The VM instances for which port mirroring is configured must reside in the cluster where the associated flow networks are located.
portMirror.field.name.tooltip:
### Port Mirroring
1. Port mirroring mirrors the data traffic of VM NICs and sends the data traffic to the target ports. This allows for the analysis of data packets of ports and simplifies the monitoring and management of data traffic. 
2. A port mirroring instance occupies a dedicated flow network. You can create multiple sessions for a port mirroring instance.

portMirror.glossary: Port mirroring mirrors the data traffic of VM NICs and sends the data traffic to the target ports. This allows for the analysis of data packets of ports and simplifies the monitoring and management of data traffic and makes it easier to locate network errors and exceptions.
portMirror.modal.delete.alert.danger: Deleting a port mirroring instance will also delete all sessions of the instance. Proceed with caution.
portMirrorSession.field.name.tooltip:

The power status of a host.

1. After you added a host to the platform, by default, the host is in IPMI unmanaged status, which means the platform cannot obtain the power status of the host.

2. After you modify the IPMI information of a host, the host is managed by the platform through IPMI. The platform can obtain the power status of the managed host, including powered on, powered off, powering on, powering off, and unknown.

preConfigurationTemplate.field.content.t:
### Template Import

1. File format:
    - Supports uploading custom template files encoded in UTF-8.
    - Recommended file size: less than or equal to 50 KB.

2. Variable definitions:
   - System variables (All uppercase, underscore-separated): REPO_URL, USERNAME, PASSWORD, NETWORK_CFGS, FORCE_INSTALL, PRE_SCRIPTS, POST_SCRIPTS
   - Custom variables (All lowercase, underscore-separated): hostname, keyboard, timezone

3. Template syntax rules:
    - kickstart: Refer to Red Hat official documentation.
    - preseed/autoinstall: Refer to Ubuntu official documentation.
    - autoyast: Refer to SUSE official documentation.

Note: Custom bare metal templates must strictly follow the syntax rules of the corresponding selected template type.
preConfigurationTemplate.field.operating:
### Operating System

Select a template OS for unattended deployment.

- Supports custom platform-optimized OS.
- Supports major Linux distributions, such as RHEL/CentOS series, Debian/Ubuntu series, and SUSE/openSUSE series.
### Template Type

The template type must match the selected operating system.

- Custom platform-optimized OS: Select kickstart.
- RHEL/CentOS series: Select kickstart.
- Debian/Ubuntu series: Select preseed.
- Ubuntu Live: Select autoinstall.
- SUSE/openSUSE series: Select autoyast.

### Storage Addition Method

- New: Creates a brand new data storage by initializing an unused LUN into a data storage usable by the platform. You can choose whether to clear existing data on the LUN device during addition.
- Register: Imports LUNs that already contain data (for example, storage migrated from another platform or replicated through disaster recovery) into the platform. primaryStorage.field.type.tooltip:
### Type  
7 types of primary storage are available: LocalStorage, NFS, SharedMountPoint, Ceph, SharedBlock, Vhost, and CBD.

1. LocalStorage: Uses the hard disks of each host for storage, and can work with ImageStore and SFTP image storage. The total capacity of a LocalStorage primary storage is the sum of each host directory capacity.

2. NFS: Uses network file systems for storage, and can work with ImageStore and SFTP image storage. The NFS directory is automatically mounted to all hosts.

3. SharedMountPoint: Uses shared file systems for storage, and can work with ImageStore and SFTP image storage. Supported file systems: SAN, GlusterFS, OCFS2, and GFS2. To use a SharedMountPoint primary storage, mount it to the same directory on each host in advance.

4. Ceph: Uses Ceph distributed block storage for storage, and can work with image storage in the same Ceph cluster.

5. SharedBlock: Uses LUN devices for storage, and can work with ImageStore. You can add one or more LUN devices. Note that you need to enter the unique disk identifier, such as UUID, WWN, and WWID.

6. Vhost: Uses vhost-user mode to connect with high-performance SSD distributed storage, and can work with ImageStore.

7. CBD: Connects high-performance distributed block storage through the CBD interface and can work with ImageStore.
primaryStorage.field.type.tooltip.case.h:
### Type
9 types of primary storage are available: LocalStorage, NFS, SharedMountPoint, Ceph, SharedBlock, Vhost, CBD, AliyunNAS, and AliyunEBS.

1. LocalStorage: Uses the hard disks of each host for storage, and can work with ImageStore and SFTP image storage. The total capacity of a LocalStorage primary storage is the sum of each host directory capacity.

2. NFS: Uses network file systems for storage, and can work with ImageStore and SFTP image storage. The NFS directory is automatically mounted to all hosts.

3. SharedMountPoint: Uses shared file systems for storage, and can work with ImageStore and SFTP image storage. Supported file systems: SAN, GlusterFS, OCFS2, and GFS2. To use a SharedMountPoint primary storage, mount it to the same directory on each host in advance.

4. Ceph: Uses Ceph distributed block storage for storage, and can work with image storage in the same Ceph cluster.

5. SharedBlock: Uses LUN devices for storage, and can work with ImageStore. You can add one or more LUN devices. Note that you need to enter the unique disk identifier, such as UUID, WWN, and WWID.

6. Vhost: Uses vhost-user mode to connect with high-performance SSD distributed storage, and can work with ImageStore.

7. CBD: Connects high-performance distributed block storage through the CBD interface and can work with ImageStore.

8. AliyunNAS:

    - Uses Alibaba Cloud NAS file system for storage, and can work with ImageStore.
    - Before you can use an AliyunNAS primary storage, configure the following on the Hybrid Cloud page: the Alibaba Cloud service gateway, the corresponding AccessKey, the Alibaba Cloud NAS file system, the corresponding permission groups and rules, and the whitelist mechanism for the file system.

9. AliyunEBS:

    - Uses Alibaba Cloud Elastic Block Storage (EBS) for storage, and can work with AliyunEBS image storage.
    - Before you can use an AliyunEBS primary storage, configure the following on the Hybrid Cloud page: the corresponding AccessKey, region, and zone.

ps.storage.info.tooltip:
### Capacity Info

#### I. Utilization

Displays the storage capacity and usage in the data storage.

1. Storage Utilization = Physical Used ÷ Physical Total
2. Physical Available = Physical Total − Physical Used − Safety Threshold Capacity 
3. Safety Threshold Capacity = Physical Total × (1 − Storage Utilization Threshold)

#### II. Allocation Ratio

Displays the storage allocations in the data storage.

1. Allocation Ratio = Allocated : Total Overcommit Capacity
2. Total Overcommit Capacity = Physical Total − Reserved Physical Capacity
3. Total Allocatable = Total Overcommit Capacity × Overcommit Ratio
4. Free to Allocate = Total Allocatable − Allocated

Note: When reserving local storage, the reserved capacity should be the sum of the reserved capacities of each host. It is recommended that when setting the reserved capacity, it should not exceed the total physical storage capacity of the hosts.

#### III. Distribution

Displays the storage distribution after overcommitted in the data storage. For more information, see *Capacity Calculation Rules*.

1. Storage Overcommitted Total = Reserved Capacity + Total Allocatable Storage Capacity

Note: In distributed storage, when OSDs are reused across multiple storage pools, a situation may arise where the physical capacity appears to be greater than the underlying disk capacity.

resource.config.description.premiumClust: Specifies whether to enable Zero Copy for a cluster. Enabling the feature will reduce the number of data copies between user space and kernel space, lower CPU usage, and improve vNIC performance.

Specifies whether to enable hugepages for a cluster. Default: false. If set to true, hugepages is enabled for all hosts in the cluster, with a size of 2 MB for each page. In addition, hugepage space is allocated to VM instances.

Note:

1. Before you enable hugepages for a cluster, make sure that all hosts in the cluster are in maintenance mode.
2. If you enable or disable hugepages for a cluster, you need to restart the hosts in the cluster for the change to take effect.
3. If hugepages is enabled for a cluster and you modify the memory of a host in the cluster, you need to re-enable hugepages and restart the host to make the hugepages feature take effect. 
4. If you enable hugepages for a cluster and the reserved memory size of a host in the cluster is smaller than 4 GB, the reserved memory size of the host is automatically increased to 4 GB. In addition, the rest of the memory in the host is allocated to hugepage memory.
5. Hugepage memory can be used only by VM instances. You need to set a reasonable reserved memory size for hosts. A too-small reserved memory may cause system service exceptions of hosts. If you deploy a hyper-converged environment, you need to reserve memory for OSD processes, management node services, systems, and other processes. For example, if you use 5 OSD processes, we recommend that you set the reserved memory size to 50 GB. This number includes 25 GB for OSD processes, 15 GB for management node services and systems, and 10 GB for storage management.
6. If you enable Cluster Hugepages, you cannot enable Memory Balloon or Kernel Same-Page Merging for the VM instances in this cluster. VM Memory Balloon and Kernel Same-Page Merging that have been enabled go invalid on VM instances.

This is used to set the placement policy for disks and snapshots on SAN storage LUNs. The default policy is sorting by drive letter. The available optional policies are: sort by drive letter, create disks on the LUN with the most remaining capacity, and create disks on the LUN with the fewest disks.

Takes effects on resources (VM instances and VPC vRouters) enabled with Cluster Binding in this cluster. Default: Soft Binding.

1. Soft Binding: Makes the VM instances and VPC vRouters only start in this cluster by default. If the cluster physical resources are insufficient, the VM instances and VPC vRouters may fail to start. However, you can manually migrate the VM instances and VPC vRouters to another cluster.
2. Hard Binding: Makes the VM instances and VPC vRouter can start onlt in this cluster. If the cluster physical resources are insufficient, the VM instances and VPC vRouters may fail to start. In addition, you cannot manually migrate the VM instances and VPC vRouters to another cluster.
3. This setting does not take effect on the VM instances/VPC vRouters whose Cluster Binding is disabled.

resource.config.tooltip.shared.block.all:
### Volume Space Preallocation Policy

The space preallocation policy for volumes in the current primary storage. Valid values: none and metadata.

1. none: Do not use a preallocation policy.
2. metadata: Thin provision. When a volume is created, the primary storage allocates it with a space that is required by its metadata only. Then, with more data written in, the storage dynamically allocates space for these data.
3. If you set a preallocation policy for the current primary storage, the global setting does not take effect on this primary storage.
resource.config.tooltip.shared.mount.poi:
### Volume Space Preallocation Policy

The preallocation policy for volumes in the current primary storage. Default: none. Valid values: none, metadata, falloc, and full.

1. none: Do not use a preallocation policy.
2. metadata: Thin provision. When a volume is created, the primary storage allocates it with a space that is required by its metadata only. Then, with more data written in, the storage dynamically allocates space for these data.
3. falloc: Thick provision with lazy zeroed. When a volume is created, the primary allocates it with the maximum space it requires. The data existing on the physical device is not erased during the creation but will be zeroed out when the volume has data written in for the first time. 
4. full: Thick provision with eager zeroed. When a volume is created, the primary storage allocates it with the maximum space it requires. The data existing on the physical device is zeroed immediately when the volume is created.
5. If you set a preallocation policy for the current primary storage, the global setting does not take effect on this storage.
resource.config.tooltip.sharedblock.devi:
SharedBlock Storage Distribution Policy

1. The policy used to distribute a SharedBlock LUN to a volume and snapshot. Valid values: none (default), minLvCounts, and maxFreeSize.
2. If you select none, when you create a volume or snapshot, a SharedBlock LUN that has sufficient spaceis is distributed to the volume or snapshot based on the system scheduling.
3. If you select minLvCounts, when you create a volume or snapshot, the SharedBlock LUN that has the smallest total number of volumes and snapshots and has sufficient available space is distributed to the volume or snapshot.
4. If you select maxFreeSize, when you create a volume or snapshot, the SharedBlock LUN that has the the most available space is distributed to the volume or snapshot.
5. If you specifically set the LUN distribution policy for the SharedBlock primary storage, the global setting does not take effect on the primary storage.
Make sure that the Cluster Hugepages is disabled in the cluster advanced setting.

### Recovery Policy
The Cloud supports two restoration policies: Create VM Instance and Restore to Original VM Instance.
#### Create VM Instance
1. This method will create a VM instance from the current recovery point. The original one will not be affected.
2. The newly created VM instance will quickly start up for business recovery.
3. During the recovery, the newly created VM instance will be in the Restoring Data state. In this case, the VM instance can normally provide services and you can read data from and write data into this VM instance. However, the VM's own operations are limited to Launch Console only.
#### Restore to Original VM Instance
1. You can restore the CDP data to the original VM instance by creating new volumes or overwriting the current volumes.
2. After this operation is performed, the original VM instance will quickly start up for business recovery.
3. During the recovery, the original VM instance will be in the Restoring Data state. In this case, the VM instance can normally provide services and you can read data from and write data into this VM instance. However, the VM's own operations are limited to Launch Console only.
retoreVmFromCdpBackup.field.recoveryStra:
### Recovery Method

You can restore the CDP data to the original VM instance by creating new volumes or overwriting the current volumes.
### Create Volumes
1. This method will create new volumes to replace the current volumes. Data in the current volumes will be retained.
2. This method will detach the current volumes. You can view the newly created and detached volumes on the configuration tab page of the VM instance.
3. After you confirm that the restored data is reliable, you can manually delete the detached volumes to release the storage space.
4. If the original VM instance has a memory snapshot, the Cloud automatically deletes the VM memory snapshots when using the Create Volumes method.

### Overwrite Current Volumes
1. This method will overwrite the original data in the VM instance. Please exercise caution.
2. This method will keep the snapshots in the current volumes.

### Role Type
Platform role: After a platform role is bound to users, these users will have permissions of the corresponding zone. Permissions of the platform role can only take effect on the zone managed by these users.
Project role: After users and user groups are added to projects and bind project roles, these users and user groups will have permissions of these projects and can manage data in these projects.

1. The same user can let you bind two types of roles.
2. The same user can let you bind multiple platform roles and project roles.
3. In a project, if users and user groups have multiple project roles, these users and user groups will have a collection of all permissions in this project.

role.tooltip:
### Role

Assign roles to a user. The assignment determines the permissions the user has within the platform.

- A user can be assigned one or more roles.
- When a user is assigned multiples roles, the user will have a combined set of permissions from all those roles.
- When a user joins a user group, the user will inherit the roles from that group in addition to its already assigned roles.
- An admin user can only be assigned one role.

Predefined Roles

- Predefined roles for regular users:
  - VM User: Supports regular users in creating virtual machines and basic VM management.
- Predefined roles for admin users:
  - System Admin: Manages daily system operations and maintenance.
  - Security Admin: Manages users, security policies, and security attributes.
  - Auditor: Manages system event information and auditing.
  - Read-Only Role: Has read-only access to system resources without write permissions.

rule.field.createStyle.template.tooltip:
The following describes the syntax of the template:

- The parameters marked with an asterisk (*) are required.

- Priority: A smaller number indicates a higher priority. Valid values: 1001 to 2999. The priority of a rule in a rule set must be unique.

- Action: The following actions are supported:  
    accept: accepts the traffic that flows in or out of the specified VPC vRouter.    
    drop: drops the traffic that flows in or out of the specified VPC vRouter and does not respond to the client.    
    reject: rejects the traffic that flows in or out of the specified VPC vRouter and responds to the client.

- Packet Status: Optional. You can specify multiple status. If you do, separate each status with a semicolon (;). The following packet status are supported:

  new: new connection requests

  established: established connections

  invalid: unidentifiable connections

  related: new connection requests that are associated with existing connections

- Protocol: Optional. You can specify multiple protocols, including ALL, TCP, UDP, ICMP, GRE, ESP, AH, IPIP, VRRP, IPENCAP, PIM, OSPF, IGMP. If you do, separate each protocol with a semicolon (;). If you do not specify this parameter, the system specifies ALL.

- TCP Flag: Optional. This parameter is available only when you set the parameter to TCP. You can specify multiple flags, including SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, URG, and PSH. If you do, separate each flag with a semicolon (;).

- ICMP Type: Optional. This parameter is available only when you set the parameter to ICMP. Supported ICMP types include echo-reply, echo-request, destination-unreachable, source-quench, redirect, router-advertisement, router-solicitation, time-exceeded, parameter-problem, timestamp-reply, timestamp-request, address-mask-request, and address-mask-reply.

- Source Port/Destination Port: Optional. The two parameters are available only when you set the parameter to TCP or UDP. You can specify a port or port range. If you specify a port range, use a hyphen (-) to indicate the range, for example, 1-100. You can specify a maximum of 10 entries. If you do, separate each entry with a semicolon(;).

- Source IP Address/Destination IP Address: Optional. You can specify an IP address, IP range, or CIDR block. If you specify an IP range, use a hyphen (-) to indicate the range, for example, 192.168.0.1-192.168.0.100. If you specify multiple CIDR blocks, or a mix of CIDR blocks and other formats of entries, you can set the netmask of the CIDR blocks only to /24. If you specify only one CIDR block, you can set a random netmask. You can specify a maximum of 10 entries. If you do, separate each entry with a semicolon (;).

- Enable Now: Optional. Specifies whether to enable the rules after the rules are added to the Cloud. If you do not specify this parameter or set the parameter to disable, the rules are disabled after they are added to the Cloud. If you set the parameter to enable, the rules are enabled after they are added to the Cloud.

- Accept: accepts the traffic that flows in or out of the specified VPC vRouter.
- Drop: drops the traffic that flows in or out of the specified VPC vRouter and does not respond to the client.
- Reject: rejects the traffic that flows in or out of the specified VPC vRouter and responds to the client.

scheduledJob.field.snapshotType.tooltip:
### Snapshot Type

You can create a single snapshot or a snapshot group.

1. A single snapshot is the snapshot of the root volume of a VM instance.
2. A snapshot group consists of the snapshots of both the VM root volume and the data volumes attached to the VM instance. You can revert a snapshot group. Note that
      - A snapshot group created by a scheduled job does not contain a VM memory snapshot.
      - To create snapshot groups by a scheduled job, make sure that the VM root/data volumes are on Ceph primary storage. If you migrate the VM instance or its data volumes to non-Ceph primary storage or attach it with a data volume on non-Ceph primary storage, the scheduled job fails after these actions.
      - To create snapshot groups by a scheduled job, make sure that the VM instance is not attached with a shared volume. If you attach a shared volume to the VM instance, the scheduled job fails after the attachment.
3. If the VM root volume is on a Ceph primary storage, you can set Reserved Snapshots. Note that Reserved Snapshots do not include snapshots created manually.

2.  By default, an import and export rules of Type ALL are configured to specify that VM instances in the security group can access to each other. You can delete the default rules to make VM instances in the security group could not access each other.
securityGroup.detail.vmNic.toolbarHandle:
### Attach NIC

1. As an administrator, note the following points when you perform this action:
- You can attach a security group owned by administrators to any NIC. If the NIC is owned by administrators, the security group is endowed with a priority lower than those of all security groups that have been attached to the NIC by default. If the NIC is owned by a tenant or sub-account, the security group is endowed with a priority higher than those of all security groups that have been attached to the NIC.
- You can attach a security group owned by a tenant/sub-account to only NICs that are also owned by this tenant/sub-account. The security group is endowed with a priority lower than those of all security groups that have been attached to the NIC by default.
2.  As a tenant/sub-account, you can attach security groups to NICs owned by your self. The security group is endowed with a priority lower than those of all security groups that have been attached to the NIC by default.
3. After the attachment, you an enter the action lists of VM NICs and click "Set Security Group" to adjust the default priorities.
securityGroup.field.authorized.dst.toolt:
### Destination

Specify IP addresses or a security group as the target objects for egress rules:

1. IP/CIDR: Allows/denies access to the NICs within the security group from the specified IP addresses.

    - To add an IP range, use the format "Start IP-End IP."
    - To add multiple IP addresses (or ranges), separate them with commas. For example: 192.168.24.10,192.168.24.12,192.168.24.62-192.168.24.70
    - Do not use 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0

2. Security Group: Allow/reject the NICs in the current group to access NICs in another security group.
securityGroup.field.authorized.src.toolt:
### Source

Specify IP addresses or a security group as the target objects for ingress rules:

1. IP/CIDR: Allows/denies access to the NICs within the security group from the specified IP addresses.

    - To add an IP range, use the format "Start IP-End IP."
    - To add multiple IP addresses (or ranges), separate them with commas. For example: 192.168.24.10,192.168.24.12,192.168.24.62-192.168.24.70
    - Do not use 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0

2. Security Group: Allows/denies access to the NICs in the current group from NICs within another security group.

securityGroup.field.rule.egress.tooltip:
### Egress Rule

Rules that take effect on traffic flowing out of NICs. You can add one or more rules and set priorities. Note that:

1. The system automatically adds rules with the highest priority that allow mutual communications among NICs in the group. These rules cannot be deleted or modified. If you want to cancel the mutual communications, just disable these rules.

2. Except for the flows stipulated by security groups, all egress flows from the NICs in security groups are allowed by default. You can enter the NIC action list and click Set Security Group to modify this default policy.
securityGroup.field.rule.ingress.tooltip:
### Ingress Rule

1. The system automatically adds rules with the highest priority that allow mutual communications among NICs in the group. These rules cannot be deleted or modified. If you want to cancel the mutual communications, just disable these rules.

2. Except for the flows stipulated by security groups, NICs in security groups reject all ingress flows by default. You can enter the NIC action list and click Set Security Group to modify this default policy.

### Priority

sessionPersistence.cookie:
### Cookie Handling Method

The Round Robin or Weighted Round Robin algorithm supports the following two cookie handling methods:

- Insert Cookie: A load balancer inserts cookies into the messages of a backend server responded to a client, so next time when the client sends requests along with the cookies, the load balancer can direct the requests to the backend server previously responded.
- Rewrite Cookie: You need to customize a cookie in the response text returned by the backend server. After the customization, a load balancer rewrites the cookie. So next time when the client sends requests along with the cookie, the load balancer can direct the requests to the backend server previously responded.

### Memory Snapshot

snapshot.field.memory.tooltip.has.block:
### Memory Snapshot

A memory snapshot captures the real-time state of a virtual machine.

- Prerequisites:

  1. The virtual machine must be in the running state.
  2. Any attached peripheral devices must be detached from the virtual machine.
  3. You cannot take memory snapshots for virtual machines using distributed storage.

- To ensure memory consistency, the virtual machine will be briefly paused during memory snapshot creation.
snapshot.field.name: Name
snapshot.field.snapshotType.tooltip:
### Snapshot Type

You can create a single snapshot or a snapshot group.

1. A single snapshot is the snapshot of the root volume of a VM instance.

2. A snapshot group consists of the root volume snapshot, the snapshots of attached data volumes, and the memory of a VM instance. You can revert a snapshot group.

Notice:

1. Currently, you cannot create memory snapshots for VM instances that use Ceph, Vhost, or CBD storage.

2. Before you can create a memory snapshot, make sure that the VM instance is in the running state.

3. Before you can create a memory snapshot, detach the peripheral devices (if any) from the VM instance first.

4. When you create a memory snapshot, to ensure memory consistency, the VM instance will be in the paused state for seconds.
### Snapshot Type
You can create a single snapshot or a snapshot group,

1. A single snapshot is the snapshot of the root volume of a VM instance.
2. A snapshot group consists of the attached data volumes and the memory of a VM instance. You can revert a snapshot group.

Notice:

1. Currently, you cannot create memory snapshots for VM instances that use Ceph or Block primary storages.
2. Before you can create a memory snapshot, make sure that the VM instances is in the running states.
3. Before you can create a memory snapshot, detach the peripheral devices (if any) from the VM instance first.
4. When you create a memory snapshot, to ensure memory consistency, the VM instance will be in the paused state for seconds.

### Total Migration Rate

Allows you to specify the data transmission rate in a VM storage migration. Valid range: 1MB/s~100GB/s. Default value: 50MB/s.

  1. The system limits the maximum I/O read rate of each volume in the source primary storage. If the VM instance has multiple volumes attached, the total migration rate does not exceed the rate limit.

  2.  When the total migration rate is less than the number of volumes, if the calculated average migration rate limit of volumes is less than 1MB/s, the default migration rate limit will be set to 1MB/s for each volume.

  3. Please set the migration rate limit reasonably according to the actual business requirements and network storage conditions to avoid affecting normal business operations.

  4. The VM memory migration will also be affected by this migration rate. We recommend that you migrate VM instances during off-peak business hours to minimize dirty pages.

task.delete.strategy.tooltip:
### Deletion Policy

When a migration task is in the "Cutover in Progress", "Cutover Successful", or "Cutover Failed" state, the following deletion policies are available:

- **Retain target instance, delete migration task**:

Deletes only the migration task record, while the target instance is retained. You can reconfigure the source VM and start a new migration task later. This operation does not cause data or state loss, but the target instance must be managed by you.

- **Delete target instance, delete migration task**:

Deletes the migration task record and its associated target instance. You can reconfigure the source VM and start a new migration task later.

- **Delete cutover program only**:

Removes only the cutover program. This policy is only available when "Create Rollback Snapshot" is enabled. The system automatically rolls back the target instance to its state before cutover. Any changes made after cutover will be lost. This operation is irreversible. Use with caution.

third.party.auth.field.alert.warning:
### Type

You can add the following protocol-based authentication servers:

- AD: Synchronizes AD users/organizations to the Cloud platform's user list and organization architecture. Supports using specified AD user attributes for login to the Cloud platform.

- LDAP: Synchronizes LDAP users to the Cloud platform's user list. Supports using specified LDAP user attributes for login to the Cloud platform.

- OIDC: An SSO server based on the OIDC protocol. It authenticates and authorizes users from the SSO system to log in to the Cloud platform without a password and synchronizes user information to the Cloud platform based on the mapping rule.

- OAuth2: An SSO server based on the OAuth2 protocol. It authenticates and authorizes users from the SSO system to log in to the Cloud platform without a password and synchronizes user information to the Cloud platform based on the mapping rule.

- CAS: An SSO server based on the CAS protocol. It authenticates and authorizes users from the SSO system to log in to the Cloud platform without a password and synchronizes user information to the Cloud platform based on the mapping rule.

- SAML: An SSO server based on the SAML 2.0 protocol. It enables the Cloud platform (as a Service Provider, SP) to integrate with an Identity Providers (IdP). Users from the IdP can log in to the Cloud platform without a password after authentication and authorization. User information will be synchronized to the Cloud platform according to mapping rules.

third.party.auth.oidc.create.redirectTem:

    - If the selected source VM instances have a NIC: 
        - Manual configuration: You can enter a new MAC address and IP address for the destination NIC or use the MAC address and IP address of the source NIC.
        - Automatic configuration: After the migration, the MAC address of the destination NIC is consistent with that of the source NIC, and the IP address of the destination NIC is dynamically allocated by the system.
    - If the selected source VM instances have no NIC:
        - Manual configuration: You can enter a new MAC address and IP address for the destination NIC.   
        - Automatic configuration: After the migration, the MAC address and IP address of the destination NIC are dynamically allocated by the system.

### L2 Network

Maps layer 2 broadcast domains and can be used for layer 2 isolation. Generally, L2 networks are identified by device numbers. The following types of L2 networks are supported:

L2NoVlanNetwork:
1. Indicates that VLAN is not configured for network devices mapping the associated hosts.
2. If a switch port is configured with VLAN, set the Access mode on the switch side.
3. If a switch port is not configured with VLAN, no other specific settings are required.
4. When an L2 network is created, a bridge device will be created based on the network device that you entered.

 L2VlanNetwork:
1. Indicates that VLAN is configured for network devices mapping the associated hosts.
2. Set the Trunk mode for the switch sides where hosts are connected.
3. Virtual local area networks are logically divided, and 1-4094 subnets are supported.
4. When L2 networks are created, VLAN devices will be created based on the network devices that you entered. Besides, bridges will be created based on these VLAN devices.
